workload.description: Read-dominated publishing platform; the CDN absorbs 80% of article reads at the edge

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: m6i.large — AWS EC2 us-east-1 / On-Demand / Linux / shared tenancy / 730 h per month; instance-hour only (excludes EBS, data transfer); x86-64 (Intel Ice Lake). Band: zero-width: within the pinned scope the hourly list rate is a single exact published number with no variance. Month length (672-744 h), burstable credit surcharges, Savings Plans and Spot are OUT-OF-BAND modifiers, named per row, not band edges.

citations.note: $0.096/h x 730 = 7008c/month. Cross-checked to the cent against the AWS Price List Bulk API (version 20260904231117).

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: cache.t4g.medium — AWS ElastiCache us-east-1 / On-Demand / Redis engine / standard support / 730 h per month; node-hour only. Band: zero-width at the Redis/Memcached standard-support rate. The Valkey engine is CHEAPER and Extended Support is DEARER; both are different products/support states, not a price range for this row, so they are named here rather than used as band edges.

db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class.

components.name: Read replica — article and feed reads

monthly_cost_per_instance.measured_context: db.m6i.large — AWS RDS PostgreSQL us-east-1 / On-Demand / Single-AZ (band high = Multi-AZ) / 730 h per month; INSTANCE-HOURS ONLY (excludes storage, provisioned IOPS and backup above the free allocation). Band: deployment spread: low = Single-AZ, high = Multi-AZ. Both are on-demand, standard-tier, us-east-1 PostgreSQL, so the band is fully in scope. Multi-AZ is ~2x Single-AZ.

citations.note: $0.178/h Single-AZ x 730 = 12994c/month. MySQL/MariaDB run ~3.9% cheaper than PostgreSQL for the same class. A read replica is billed as its own full instance, at the same rate as a primary.

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 8,000 req/s peak AT THE EDGE. 85% article reads, 10% feed listings, 5% writes (comments and publishes). Writes bypass the CDN entirely

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: 80% edge hit-rate on articles, 50% on feeds — feeds change on every publish, articles almost never. VISIT PROBABILITIES ARE CUMULATIVE from the flow entry: the origin sees 0.20 of article reads, and the replica 0.04 (a CDN miss AND a cache miss)

assumptions.subject: cache
assumptions.statement: Behind the CDN, 80% of origin article reads are served from the rendered-page cache; only 4% of all article reads reach the database tier

assumptions.subject: app
assumptions.statement: ~900 req/s per instance for a cache miss (fetch, render, serialise). Three instances hold the origin at 80% - but that is 80% of the MISS traffic. If the CDN goes cold, the article path alone jumps from 0.20 to 1.00 (5x) and the origin as a whole goes from 2,160 to 8,000 req/s, ~3.7x its design load. This tier is the first thing to fall over

assumptions.subject: cdn
assumptions.statement: Egress 150,000 GB/month is derived, not observed: the CDN itself serves ~7,600 responses/s at peak, an assumed 30% average-to-peak ratio gives ~2,280/s, and at ~25 KB per response that is ~148,000 GB/month, rounded to 150,000. TEXT ONLY - images and video are assumed to be served by a separate media pipeline that is not part of this model

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Egress is charged at the default $0.09/GB internet list rate. A platform at this volume negotiates CDN rates several times lower; treat the egress line as a ceiling

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: CDN per-REQUEST charges are set to zero on purpose. The engine carries one request rate and it is API-gateway shaped ($3.00 per million); CloudFront-class request pricing is roughly $0.75-1.00 per million, so billing ~5.9 billion edge requests at the gateway rate would overstate that line by 3-4x. A real bill adds roughly $4,000-6,000/month here. Egress is modelled; requests are a named gap

_library.summary: Read-dominated publishing platform where the CDN absorbs most article traffic before the origin.
